---
title: "Team"
subtitle: "Who does what across the project"
---

The project brings together investigators at seven institutions on the Atlantic, Gulf, and Pacific coasts, each leading one or more of the hatchery, field, mechanistic, phenotyping, economics, and extension components. Coordination happens through an Executive Committee that meets quarterly.

<!-- To add a photo for a person, drop a square image in assets/people/ and add

## Project Team

### Chris Anderson
**University of Washington**

Leads the Economics and Decision Tools team: the portfolio-optimization dashboard and regional cost–benefit analyses under Objective 3, plus the aquaculture-economics curriculum.

### Mackenzie Gavery
**NOAA Northwest Fisheries Science Center**

Co-leads the predictive-phenotyping cross-cutting team and physiological assay development. Manages the Pacific Hybreed co-production partnership at NOAA Manchester.

### Samuel Gurr
**Oregon State University / USDA ARS**

Leads resazurin metabolic profiling and thermal performance curves for Objective 2, and serves as supervisory lead for four hatchery-based research assistants.

### Chris Hollenbeck
**Texas A&M / CMAQ**

Directs Gulf-coast research. Leads Objective 1 experiments on *C. virginica* low-salinity tolerance and resilience, Gulf field deployments, and extension in coordination with Texas Sea Grant.

### Joseph Matt
**Texas A&M**

Leads Gulf Objective 1 execution: priming treatments, acute stress challenges, and field performance monitoring.

### Louis Plough
**USDA ARS / POGS**

Directs Pacific-coast research. Leads Objective 1 experiments on *C. gigas* POMS/OsHV-1 resistance using POGS families, Oregon and Washington field deployments, and Oregon Sea Grant extension.

### David Portnoy
**Texas A&M**

Leads the high-throughput genotyping behind Gulf Objective 1, including family assignment and the population-genomic analyses that support it.

### Steven Roberts
**University of Washington**

Coordinates project-wide administration and reporting, chairs the Executive Committee, and serves as primary NIFA liaison. Leads machine-learning modeling and cross-site data integration, the PRISM Portal, and Pacific-coast co-production partnerships.

### Hamish Small
**Virginia Institute of Marine Science**

Leads work on the mechanisms of environmental memory, including the role of DNA methylation in priming and the duration of signaling, embedded in ABC breeding-program sampling.

### Jessica Small
**Virginia Institute of Marine Science / ABC**

Directs Atlantic-coast hatchery operations and leads Objective 1 G×E×P experiments in *C. virginica*. Integrates project findings into VIMS coursework and workforce training.

### William Walton
**Virginia Institute of Marine Science**

Leads extension across the project. Runs Objective 1 field trials and Objective 2 activities on the Atlantic, and coordinates Virginia and North Carolina grow-out partners and mid-Atlantic producer engagement.

## Trainees

The project supports nine graduate students and postdoctoral researchers with cross-institutional rotations, and engages more than 20 undergraduates over the award period.
